c.tagline: Green coastal capital at the easternmost point of the Americas.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are metered, but app rides via Uber and 99 are usually cheaper and easier, especially from the airport.

emergency.note: 190 reaches the Military Police, 192 the SAMU ambulance service and 193 the fire brigade. 911 is not used in Brazil.

avoid.reason: Caution outside the main beaches at night

hood_desc: The city's main tourist beach and hub, home to the landmark Hotel Tambaú, the craft fair, seafood restaurants and calm reef-protected swimming; the most convenient, walkable base for first-timers.
The southern beachfront district crowned by the Cabo Branco lighthouse and Ponta do Seixas, the easternmost point of the Americas, plus Oscar Niemeyer's Estação Cabo Branco; scenic and relaxed.
The upscale, buzzing district just north of Tambaú with the city's best nightlife, bars, restaurants and the Manaíra Shopping mall; lively after dark and popular with visitors.
A newer, largely residential beach neighborhood at the north end with wide quiet sands, the 'Caribessa' natural pools offshore and a local, family feel; calm and less touristy.
The UNESCO-recognized colonial old town on the Sanhauá River with the São Francisco cultural complex, baroque churches and pastel townhouses; the historic and cultural heart, best visited by day.

water.note: Tap water is treated but most locals drink filtered or bottled; visitors should stick to bottled.

transit.hours: City buses run from roughly 5:00 AM to around midnight; late-night travel relies on Uber, 99 and taxis.
transit.note: João Pessoa has no metro or tram; getting around means the municipal bus network plus ride-hailing apps and taxis. The beach neighborhoods of Tambaú, Cabo Branco and Manaíra are compact and pleasant to walk.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the onboard conductor or with a rechargeable Passe Legal card; app rides and taxis take cash or card.

bus: Intercity coaches to Recife, Natal and other cities from the Rodoviária
train: No urban rail; intercity travel is by coach or air

transit.m: Municipal bus toward the city center/beaches (~40-50 min)
Taxi to Tambaú/Manaíra beach area (20-30 min)

tip.r: A 10% service charge is usually added to restaurant bills; anything beyond that is optional.

landmarks: Centro Cultural São Francisco (São Francisco Church and Convent)
One of Brazil's finest baroque ensembles, this gilded 16th-century Franciscan church and convent dazzles with Portuguese azulejos and a theatrical courtyard cross.
Farol do Cabo Branco (Cape Branco Lighthouse)
A striking modernist lighthouse crowning red cliffs near Ponta do Seixas, the easternmost point of the Americas, where Brazil greets the sunrise first.
Estação Cabo Branco (Ciência, Cultura e Artes)
Oscar Niemeyer's swooping white saucer of a cultural center hovers above the coast, hosting exhibitions and panoramic terraces over the Atlantic.
Praia de Tambaú
The city's signature urban beach, its palm-fringed promenade, craft stalls and calm reef-sheltered waters buzzing from breakfast tapioca to evening coconuts.
Praia do Jacaré (Jacaré Beach Sunset)
Every dusk on the Paraíba River, a saxophonist drifts by boat playing Ravel's Boléro as crowds toast one of Brazil's most famous sunsets.
Parque Solon de Lucena (Lagoa)
A perfectly circular lagoon ringed by towering royal palms in the city center, João Pessoa's postcard park for jogging, cycling and people-watching.
Areia Vermelha Sandbank
At low tide a crimson-sand island surfaces offshore, and catamarans deliver bathers to natural pools, floating bars and starfish-studded shallows.
Picãozinho Natural Pools
Boat trips from Tambaú reach these coral reef pools at low tide, where snorkelers drift among rainbow fish in waist-deep turquoise water.
Basílica de Nossa Senhora das Neves
The city's mother church, founded with the town in 1585 and rebuilt in graceful style, honors the snow-titled patroness of one of Brazil's oldest cities.
Hotel Globo and the Historic Center
A restored 1920s hotel-turned-cultural space whose terrace delivers the classic sunset view over the Sanhauá River and the pastel colonial old town.

train.note: No intercity passenger trains. A CBTU commuter line runs west to Cabedelo and Santa Rita, which is handy locally but not for travel between cities. Long-distance journeys are by coach or plane.

bus.note: No international coaches. The Rodoviária is west of the centre, with frequent services to Recife (about 2 hours), Natal (3) and Campina Grande, run by Progresso and Nordeste and bookable through ClickBus (https://www.clickbus.com.br/). City buses reach the Tambaú beachfront and Ponta do Seixas, the easternmost point of the Americas.

ferry.note: There is no scheduled passenger ferry. Boats from Jacaré and Cabedelo run sunset and reef trips and catamarans go out to the Areia Vermelha sandbank at low tide, all as excursions rather than transport.

half.name: Praia de Tambaba (Conde)
half.blurb: A cliff-backed beach in Conde with a clothing-optional section, about an hour south of João Pessoa.

half.name: Praia do Coqueirinho (Conde)
half.blurb: A beach flanked by red-clay cliffs and natural tide pools, near Tambaba, about an hour south of João Pessoa.

half.name: Baía da Traição
half.blurb: A fishing village and Potiguara indigenous reserve north of João Pessoa, known for fresh seafood and quiet beaches.

full.name: Areia
full.blurb: A colonial hill town in the Brejo Paraibano highlands with preserved sugar-plantation mansions, about two hours from João Pessoa.
